# Loco — full reference for building apps (0.17.x)

This is a complete, single-file guide for building **Loco** (loco.rs)
applications, sized for large-context models. Loco is an all-in-one,
batteries-included Rust web framework — "Rails for Rust". One binary and one set
of conventions give you routing, a Sea-ORM database layer, background jobs, a
scheduler, mailers, tasks, storage, caching, and testing.

Version target: **Loco 0.17.x** — Sea-ORM 2.0, sqlx 0.9, edition 2021,
64-bit (`i64`) primary keys. Prose docs: https://loco.rs/docs.

The prime directive: **Loco already integrates the infrastructure. Prefer its
built-ins and generators over adding external crates and wiring servers, pools,
or job runners by hand.** Everything is reached through `AppContext` (`ctx`).

---

## 1. Bootstrapping a project

```sh
# install the generator CLI
cargo install loco

# create an app (interactive wizard: SaaS/API/lightweight, DB, workers, assets)
loco new

# run it
cd myapp
cargo loco start
```

A generated app has this shape:

```
src/
  app.rs             # impl Hooks for App: the wiring hub
  bin/main.rs        # entrypoint
  controllers/       # HTTP handlers grouped into Routes
  models/
    _entities/       # GENERATED Sea-ORM entities — do not hand-edit
    *.rs             # your model logic
  views/             # response shaping
  workers/           # background jobs
  tasks/             # one-off/CLI tasks
  mailers/           # email
  initializers/      # startup hooks
migration/           # Sea-ORM migration crate
config/              # development.yaml / production.yaml / test.yaml
tests/               # request/model/task tests
assets/ frontend/    # static/SPA (optional)
```

## 2. The `Hooks` trait (`src/app.rs`) — the wiring hub

Everything becomes active by being registered here. Generators update this file
for you; when wiring by hand, this is the file to edit.

```rust
use loco_rs::prelude::*;

pub struct App;

#[async_trait]
impl Hooks for App {
    fn app_name() -> &'static str { env!("CARGO_CRATE_NAME") }

    fn routes(_ctx: &AppContext) -> AppRoutes {
        AppRoutes::with_default_routes()
            .add_route(controllers::posts::routes())
            .add_route(controllers::auth::routes())
    }

    async fn connect_workers(ctx: &AppContext, queue: &Queue) -> Result<()> {
        queue.register(workers::downloader::DownloadWorker::build(ctx)).await?;
        Ok(())
    }

    fn register_tasks(tasks: &mut Tasks) {
        tasks.register(tasks::user_report::UserReport);
    }

    // migrations, initializers, truncate/seed for tests, etc.
}
```

## 3. `AppContext` — the service hub

Passed to handlers, workers, tasks, and initializers. Key fields:

- `ctx.db` — Sea-ORM `DatabaseConnection`.
- `ctx.config` — the loaded per-environment `Config`.
- `ctx.mailer` — the configured mailer (if enabled).
- `ctx.storage` — object storage (local/S3/Azure/GCS via OpenDAL).
- `ctx.cache` — cache (in-memory or Redis).
- `ctx.queue_provider` — the background-job queue.

Never construct your own DB pool, HTTP server, mailer, or job queue — read them
from `ctx`.

## 4. Models & migrations (Sea-ORM 2.0)

Generate a model (writes a migration and regenerates the entity):

```sh
cargo loco generate model posts title:string content:text published:bool user:references
cargo loco db migrate      # apply
cargo loco db entities     # regenerate entities from the DB schema
```

Field types include `string`, `text`, `int`, `big_int`, `bool`, `ts`, `tstz`,
`uuid`, `decimal`, `json`, `jsonb`, `references` (FK). Suffixes: `!` = required
(non-null), `^` = unique. **Primary keys and `references` are `i64` (BIGINT) in
0.17+.**

Entities are generated into `src/models/_entities/<name>.rs`. Put custom logic
in `src/models/<name>.rs`:

```rust
use loco_rs::prelude::*;
use super::_entities::posts::{ActiveModel, Entity, Model, Column};

#[async_trait::async_trait]
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {
    async fn before_save<C: ConnectionTrait>(self, _db: &C, insert: bool)
        -> std::result::Result<Self, DbErr> { Ok(self) }
}

impl Model {
    pub async fn find_by_title(db: &DatabaseConnection, title: &str) -> Result<Option<Self>> {
        Ok(Entity::find().filter(Column::Title.eq(title)).one(db).await?)
    }
}
```

Common queries:

```rust
Entity::find_by_id(id).one(&ctx.db).await?;                 // Option<Model>
Entity::find().all(&ctx.db).await?;                         // Vec<Model>
Entity::find().filter(Column::Published.eq(true)).all(&ctx.db).await?;

let mut item = ActiveModel { title: Set("hi".to_string()), ..Default::default() };
let item = item.insert(&ctx.db).await?;                     // create
let mut a = item.into_active_model(); a.title = Set("x".into()); a.update(&ctx.db).await?;
```

Pagination returns a `PageResponse<T>` whose metadata is in
`response.meta` (`meta.page`, `meta.page_size`, `meta.total_pages`,
`meta.total_items`) in 0.17+.

Sea-ORM 2.0 note: raw-`Statement` execution uses `_raw`-suffixed methods
(`execute_raw`, `query_one_raw`, `query_all_raw`). Migrations pass SeaQuery
statements by reference; the generators emit correct code.

## 5. Controllers, routing, extractors, responses

```rust
use loco_rs::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use crate::models::_entities::posts::{ActiveModel, Entity, Model};

#[derive(Deserialize, Serialize)]
pub struct Params { pub title: String, pub content: Option<String> }

async fn load_item(ctx: &AppContext, id: i64) -> Result<Model> {
    Entity::find_by_id(id).one(&ctx.db).await?.ok_or_else(|| Error::NotFound)
}

pub async fn list(State(ctx): State<AppContext>) -> Result<Response> {
    format::json(Entity::find().all(&ctx.db).await?)
}

pub async fn get_one(Path(id): Path<i64>, State(ctx): State<AppContext>) -> Result<Response> {
    format::json(load_item(&ctx, id).await?)
}

pub async fn add(State(ctx): State<AppContext>, Json(params): Json<Params>) -> Result<Response> {
    let item = ActiveModel { title: Set(params.title), ..Default::default() };
    format::json(item.insert(&ctx.db).await?)
}

pub fn routes() -> Routes {
    Routes::new()
        .prefix("api/posts/")
        .add("/", get(list))
        .add("/", post(add))
        .add("{id}", get(get_one))
}
```

- Handlers are `async fn(...) -> Result<Response>`. Extractors: `State(ctx):
  State<AppContext>`, `Path(id): Path<i64>`, `Json(body): Json<T>`,
  `Query(q): Query<T>`, plus Loco's `JsonValidate`/`JsonValidateWithMessage`
  (validate with the `validator` derive), `RemoteIP`, `SharedStore`, auth
  extractors (`auth::JWT`, `auth::ApiToken`).
- Responses: `format::json(x)`, `format::html(s)`, `format::empty()`, or the
  view layer. Errors: return `Error::NotFound`, `Error::Unauthorized(..)`,
  `bad_request(..)`, `unauthorized(..)`, etc.
- Register the `Routes` in `app.rs` `Hooks::routes` via
  `.add_route(controllers::posts::routes())`.
- Middleware (CORS, compression, timeouts, secure headers, limits, etc.) is
  configured in `config/*.yaml` under `server.middlewares`.

## 6. Background workers

```rust
use loco_rs::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Debug)]
pub struct DownloadWorkerArgs { pub user_id: i64 }

pub struct DownloadWorker;

#[async_trait]
impl BackgroundWorker<DownloadWorkerArgs> for DownloadWorker {
    fn build(ctx: &AppContext) -> Self { Self }
    async fn perform(&self, args: DownloadWorkerArgs) -> Result<()> {
        // do work using services from the captured ctx
        Ok(())
    }
}
```

Enqueue:

```rust
let job_id = DownloadWorker::perform_later(&ctx, DownloadWorkerArgs { user_id }).await?;
DownloadWorker::perform_later_with_priority(&ctx, args, Some(42)).await?; // higher = sooner
```

- Backends: Postgres (`bg_pg`), SQLite (`bg_sqlt`), Redis (`bg_redis`). Choose
  via config `workers.mode` (`BackgroundQueue` / `BackgroundAsync` /
  `ForegroundBlocking`) and `queue.kind`. Register in
  `Hooks::connect_workers`.
- **0.17+:** `perform_later` returns the job id (`Result<String>`); priority is
  supported on all backends (mailer jobs default to `100`); the **Redis backend
  moved from Lists to Sorted Sets** — drain old Redis queues before upgrading.
- Run workers: `cargo loco start --worker` (dedicated) or
  `--server-and-worker`, or `--all`.

## 7. Scheduler

Define in `config/*.yaml`:

```yaml
scheduler:
  jobs:
    write_content:
      run: "echo hello"      # a shell command, or a registered task
      shell: true
      cron: "*/5 * * * *"
```

Run with `cargo loco scheduler` or `cargo loco start --scheduler` (0.17+ lets
you run the scheduler without a worker).

## 8. Mailers

```sh
cargo loco generate mailer auth
```

```rust
use loco_rs::prelude::*;

impl Mailer for AuthMailer {}
impl AuthMailer {
    pub async fn send_welcome(ctx: &AppContext, to: &str) -> Result<()> {
        Self::mail_template(ctx, &EMAIL_TEMPLATE, mailer::Args {
            to: to.to_string(),
            locals: serde_json::json!({}),
            ..Default::default()
        }).await
    }
}
```

Mailer jobs are enqueued (default priority `100`). Configure SMTP in config,
including implicit TLS:

```yaml
mailer:
  smtp:
    host: smtp.example.com
    port: 465
    tls: implicit               # or "starttls" / "none"; secure:true == starttls
    auth:
      user: "{{ get_env(name='SMTP_USER') }}"
      password: "{{ get_env(name='SMTP_PASSWORD') }}"
```

## 9. Tasks

```rust
use loco_rs::prelude::*;

pub struct UserReport;

#[async_trait]
impl Task for UserReport {
    fn task(&self) -> TaskInfo {
        TaskInfo { name: "user_report".to_string(), detail: "generate a report".to_string() }
    }
    async fn run(&self, ctx: &AppContext, vars: &task::Vars) -> Result<()> {
        // full AppContext available
        Ok(())
    }
}
```

Register in `Hooks::register_tasks`; run with `cargo loco task user_report`.

## 10. Configuration

`config/{development,production,test}.yaml`, selected by `LOCO_ENV`. Read via
`ctx.config`. Secrets come from the environment through the `get_env` Tera
helper **inside the YAML**, not scattered `std::env::var` calls. Typical
sections: `server`, `database`, `queue`, `workers`, `mailer`, `auth`,
`logger`, `scheduler`, `storage`, `cache`, `settings` (your app-specific
values).

## 11. Storage & cache

- `ctx.storage` — unified object storage over OpenDAL: in-memory, filesystem,
  S3, Azure Blob, GCS. `ctx.storage.upload(path, &bytes).await?`,
  `.download(path)`, `.delete(path)`, plus streaming.
- `ctx.cache` — `ctx.cache.get_or_insert(...)`, `.insert`, `.get`, `.remove`;
  in-memory (moka) or Redis backend.

## 12. Testing

```rust
use loco_rs::testing::prelude::*;

#[tokio::test]
#[serial]
async fn can_list_posts() {
    request::<App>(|request, _ctx| async move {   // 0.17+: ::<App>, not ::<App, _, _>
        let res = request.get("/api/posts/").await;
        assert_eq!(res.status_code(), 200);
    })
    .await;
}
```

- Helpers (0.17+ take `impl AsyncFnOnce`): `request::<App>`,
  `request_with_config::<App>`, `request_with_create_db::<App>`,
  `request_config_with_create_db::<App>`.
- DB tests use `request_with_create_db`, seed via fixtures, and assert with
  `insta` snapshots. Mark DB tests `#[serial]`.
- Model/task tests use `boot_test`/`testing::prelude` helpers and a seeded DB.

## 13. CLI reference

```
cargo loco start [--server-and-worker | --worker | --scheduler | --all]
cargo loco generate model|scaffold|controller|worker|task|scheduler|mailer|migration|deployment
cargo loco db migrate|entities|reset|seed|status
cargo loco task <name> [key:value ...]
cargo loco scheduler
cargo loco routes
cargo loco doctor          # verify environment, DB, and tool versions
cargo loco version
```

## 14. Upgrading 0.16 → 0.17 (highlights)

- **Sea-ORM 2.0 + sqlx 0.9** — bump `sea-orm`/`sea-orm-migration` to `2.0` and
  `sqlx` to `0.9`; update `sea-orm-cli`; regenerate entities. Raw-`Statement`
  calls gain `_raw`.
- **64-bit keys** — generated `id`/`references` are now `i64` (BIGINT). Only
  affects newly generated code; existing tables are untouched.
- **`perform_later` returns the job id**; new `perform_later_with_priority`.
- **Priority queues** — Postgres/SQLite auto-migrate a `priority` column; **the
  Redis backend switched Lists → Sorted Sets (drain old Redis queues first).**
- **`PageResponse` carries `meta: PagerMeta`** instead of flat fields.
- **`request::<App>`** — test helpers take `impl AsyncFnOnce` (drop `, _, _`).
- **`loco_rs::Error` is `#[non_exhaustive]`** — add a `_ =>` arm to exhaustive
  matches.
- Dependency majors bumped (thiserror 2, tower 0.5, redis 1, opendal 0.57,
  etc.); most are transitive for apps. Full details:
  https://loco.rs/docs/extras/upgrades/.

## 15. Common pitfalls (avoid)

- ❌ Adding axum/sqlx/tokio/lettre/a job runner directly and wiring servers/pools
  by hand → ✅ use `ctx` and generators.
- ❌ Hand-editing `_entities/` → ✅ generate via migrations.
- ❌ `i32` keys / `Path<i32>` → ✅ `i64` in 0.17+.
- ❌ `request::<App, _, _>` → ✅ `request::<App>`.
- ❌ Routes not registered in `app.rs` → ✅ return `Routes` and add in `Hooks::routes`.
- ❌ Custom error enums for app code → ✅ `loco_rs::Result` + `?`.
- ❌ Ad-hoc `std::env::var` → ✅ YAML config + `ctx.config` + `get_env`.

When unsure, generate the thing and read the produced code — it is the canonical
pattern for this version.
